europe_now.title: Ratko Mladić, convicted Bosnian Serb general, dies in Hague custody
europe_now.summary: Ratko Mladić, the former Bosnian Serb military leader convicted of genocide and war crimes for his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, has died at age 84 while serving a life sentence in The Hague. His death closes a chapter on one of the most significant war crimes trials in post-Yugoslav history, with mixed reactions across the Balkans.

top_stories.title: Moldova's EU accession framed as survival issue
top_stories.summary: Moldova's bid for EU membership is increasingly being portrayed by pro-European leaders as a matter of national survival, given ongoing security pressures from Russia and internal divisions over alignment with Western institutions. The country's path toward accession remains uncertain amid economic challenges and geopolitical tensions.

top_stories.title: Poland refuses nuclear hosting despite Russian threat
top_stories.summary: Poland has ruled out hosting U.S. nuclear weapons on its territory, even as regional security concerns intensify following renewed Russian aggression in Eastern Europe. The decision underscores Warsaw’s balancing act between seeking NATO reassurance and avoiding escalation.

top_stories.title: Germany’s far right taps nostalgia for communist East to propel election surge
top_stories.summary: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is leveraging nostalgia for East Germany’s socialist era to gain traction in upcoming elections, particularly in economically disadvantaged eastern states. This rhetoric taps into widespread discontent with current economic conditions and migration policies.

europe_now.title: Norway monitors King Harald's health as condition worsens
europe_now.summary: Norwegians gathered outside the royal palace as concerns grew over King Harald's deteriorating health. Officials have not yet released detailed medical updates beyond confirming the worsening condition.

europe_now.title: Death of Ratko Mladić prompts reflection on Bosnia genocide convictions
europe_now.summary: Ratko Mladić, the former Bosnian Serb general convicted of genocide for his role in the Srebrenica massacre, has died in detention in The Hague at age 84. European outlets are revisiting the crimes for which he was held accountable and the legacy of the international tribunal's work.

top_stories.title: French presidential candidates hold first debate ahead of 2027 election
top_stories.summary: France's leading presidential contenders faced off in their first debate, tested on economic policy at a major business summit. The exchange offered an early signal of how the race could shape up ahead of the 2027 vote.

top_stories.title: Von der Leyen pushes EU budget to finance strategic autonomy
top_stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has called for the EU budget to be repurposed toward funding European strategic independence. The proposal comes amid intensifying EU budget negotiations and growing pressure over how to deploy frozen Russian assets.

top_stories.title: Jellyfish swarm forces partial shutdown at French nuclear plant
top_stories.summary: A large jellyfish bloom has forced a partial shutdown of a French nuclear reactor, disrupting operations at the facility. The incident highlights the vulnerability of coastal energy infrastructure to marine conditions.
